edits.old: Its receptive field was still only about 240–300 ms, which the authors say is too short to capture long-range structure in music or prosody.

edits.why: The 240 ms and ~300 ms figures are for the TTS and multi-speaker speech models (pp.5–6: 'can only remember the last 2–3 phonemes'; F0 contours). doubts: MOS 4.21 is the WaveNet conditioned on linguistic features and F0 (Table 1); the note does not say so but the number is right.

headings.heading: ## How a diffusion model makes an image

edits.old: but it trailed the other models of its time. On CIFAR-10 it scored 4.20 bits per dimension, against 3.00 for the autoregressive PixelRNN.
edits.new: and its log-likelihood bounds held up on small datasets: higher than the best earlier model on dead-leaves images (1.49 vs 1.24 bits per pixel) and comparable to other models on MNIST. It reported no sample-quality numbers.
edits.why: Neither 4.20 nor PixelRNN (2016, later than this paper) appears in the PDF. Its only CIFAR-10 figure is a 5.4 ± 0.2 bits/pixel lower bound on unit-variance-scaled data (Table 1), so it can't be compared with bits per dimension. Table 2 and p.6 claim state of the art on dead leaves (1.489 vs 1.244 for MCGSM; higher is better) and MNIST comparable to GSN/adversarial nets. So 'trailed the other models of its time' contradicts the paper's own results. T = 1,000 for image experiments checks (App. D).

doubts: The 4.20 vs 3.00 figures may come from some later paper's comparison table (not DDPM's: the DDPM PDF text wouldn't extract to check). If the coordinator wants to keep a 'trailed later models' point, it needs that source cited.
